newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish rain not yet affecting high grains prices.
newsitem.headline: Spanish rain not yet affecting high grains prices.

text.p: Although rain finally fell on Thursday in Spain after some months of dry weather, grain prices were still high on Friday as the rainfall had not yet been sufficient, dealers said.
With more wet weather forecast, it could ease the tight supply from next week. But it was too early to say whether the rains would really affect the harvest.
"Rain is always positive, but prices are still very high and they haven't reacted yet to the small amount of water we have had," a trader in Madrid said.
"The market remains unmanageable..it's still too early to see any effect," the trader added.
Grains prices have risen sharply after weeks without rain, with feed wheat trading on Friday at around 27,000 pesetas per tonne from 25,500 on April 4.
But traders said weather forecasts suggesting further precipitation today and over the weekend might have an impact on prices next week.
"We had rains overnight, and there're places in Spain were is still raining," another Barcelona-based dealer added.
